India crop price calendar

For each crop and state, this shows the weeks of the year when mandi prices have been highest over the last ~20 years, and — working backwards from how long the crop takes to grow — when to plant so the harvest lands on that high. It assumes you sell at harvest (no storage). It is a look at past patterns, not a price forecast.

Latest reported prices

Things to keep in mind

  • If everyone follows this, it stops working. The high price exists because few farmers harvest then. If everyone plants for the same peak, the harvest floods the market and the peak collapses. Treat this as an edge for one farm, not a plan for a district.
  • Early years are patchy. Few mandis reported prices in 2005–2008, and some crops barely appear before about 2010. Years shown is how many years of usable data went into each answer — a low number means less certainty.
  • Most crop–state pairs don't have enough data. Where a state's own history is too thin, the page falls back to the all-India pattern and marks it all-India. The planting window in that case is still fitted to your state's own sowing months.
  • Prices are 2025 rupees, per quintal (100 kg). Every year is indexed to 2025 so old and new years can be compared directly — the shape comes from twenty years of history, the rupee level from 2025. 2025's own data runs January–October, so the November and December levels are what the seasonal pattern implies, not prices actually observed.
  • "Against the usual" is not a good deal or a bad one. It only says how this week's price compares with what this crop normally does in this week of the year, after taking out how expensive the whole year has been. A price 8% above the usual could still be below last month's. It is one day's average across the state's mandis, and a thin trading day can move it a lot.
  • Planting months are approximate. They come from ICAR and state-department norms, grouped into six broad agro-climatic zones, not tuned per district.
  • A state average hides local differences. Nashik is not the rest of Maharashtra. Prices near you may peak a week or two off.
  • All-India prices pool every reporting state equally and are not weighted by how much each market actually sold.
Built from CEDA Ashoka and Agmarknet mandi price history via a fixed pipeline (median across years, each year normalised to its own average, 3-week smoothing, with an STL cross-check), then priced back into 2025 rupees per quintal. No data is fetched when this page opens.
